entry.title: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets. Identifying ligands for a protein target requires searching a vast chemical space for a comparatively small set of compatible molecules.
entry.summary:
Identifying ligands for a protein target requires searching a vast chemical space for a comparatively small set of compatible molecules. Existing machine learning approaches primarily address this problem by generating candidate ligands or scoring individual protein-ligand pairs, but provide limited information about the broader chemical space compatible with a binding pocket. We introduce RangeFinder, an SE(3)-equivariant transformer pocket-level model, trained and evaluated on BioLiP2 data, that predicts ranges over nine physicochemical ligand properties directly from pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #ml-theory

entry.title: Res ipSAE adhuc loquuntur: What the directionality of predicted aligned error in cofolding models can tell us about scoring diverse molecular complexes
entry.summary:
AlphaFold 3 (AF3) and Boltz-2 estimate confidence in predicted biomolecular complexes using the interface predicted template modeling (ipTM) score, which is derived from probability distributions of predicted aligned errors (PAEs) between molecular tokens. These errors are directional: the predicted position of tokens in one molecule is evaluated relative to coordinate frames defined by tokens in another. The PAE matrix is therefore asymmetric, but AF3 reports the maximum of the two directional pairwise ipTM scores, whereas Boltz-2 reports them separately.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: CMVAE: Contrastive Supervision Improves Single-Omic Latent Manifold for Breast Cancer Survival Prognosis
entry.summary:
High-dimensional omics data are vital for fore- casting patient prognosis in oncology. While deep multi-omics learning methods are increasingly popular, they suffer from data missingness and low patient overlap across modalities. Consequently, advancing single-omic representation learning re- mains a critical yet challenging research problem.

entry.title: scRM: A single-cell foundation model trained on scRNA-seq reads
entry.summary:
To our knowledge, scRM is the first single-cell foundation model trained on sequencing reads, demonstrating that raw data pretraining is not only feasible but competitive at a fraction of the computational cost. We anticipate that scaling this framework and exploring alternative architectures will unlock biological information inaccessible to count models and extend the dataset-specific pretraining it already makes possible. The source code is available at https://github.com/altos-labs/scRM.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Leakage-Controlled Benchmarking of Variant Effect Predictors and Development of Gradient-Boosting Consensus Model
entry.summary:
Single amino acid mutations are among the most common forms of genetic variation, with effects ranging from negligible to severe disruption of protein function. Accurate quantitative evaluation of protein variants therefore represents a key challenge in medicine and protein engineering. Computational variant effect predictors (VEPs) are widely used to prioritize missense variants, yet their fair comparison is hindered by data circularity, benchmarks restricted to human clinical annotations, and limited availability of code and training data, all of which can inflate apparent performance.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.
